ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-pass-th.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-pass-th.text: What do you think you're doing, human?

ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-pass-th.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-pass-th.text: You can admire them from back here!

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: It's a bit rude of 'em to take up the whole bridge with their conversation, isn't it, mate?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 2
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: Aye, mate, but wouldn't it be just as rude for us to interrupt?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: A good point well made, mate. Who are we to decide that the dig is more impor'ant than a personal disagreement between two people?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 2
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: You're not wrong, mate. We often place matters of industry above those of people, and it's chippin' away at our ability to relate to each other on a human level.

options.text: What's going on here?

steps.player: What's going on here?

steps.speaker: Builder 1
steps.text: We're part of a dig into some ruins beneath Cam Torum, but the way's blocked by these folks.

steps.player: Have you tried asking them to move?

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: We're considering the moral implications of doing exactly that, mate.

options.text: Are you two philosophers?

steps.player: Are you two philosophers?

steps.speaker: Builder 1
steps.text: No mate, builders.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: But thinking, talking, discussing, it's what makes us human, mate.

steps.player: It's not just humans that do those things.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: Fair play, mate. I guess we're reflecting more on the condition of sen'ience in general then.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: Have a good one, mate.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: It is my right and duty as a follower of Ranul to document that which has been found beneath your city.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: Your beliefs do not grant you a right to anything in Cam Torum, not to document things, and especially not to get yourself killed.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: I don't want to give Fortis any excuses to come knocking on our door to investigate your untimely and idiotic demise.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: I won't take no for an answer. I am bound by my divine oath.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: Oh yes? And will your divine oath feed you in there? Light your way? Keep you safe from cave-ins and monsters?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.player: I don't know about cave-ins, but I can handle monsters.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: If the player does not meet the quest requirements:

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Sorry, but I'm busy with a different arrogant human. You'll have to wait in line.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Perilous Moons quest.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: If the player meets the quest requirements:

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Ranul provides...

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: No! We've more than enough humans in Cam Torum with this blasted Fortis mandated dig! I don't care how many deals it secured, it's not worth all this trouble!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Advisor Attala...

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: What?!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Apologies, but I was sent to tell you that one of the creatures from the ruins managed to bypass our defenses.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: It escaped through the mountain's outflow spring, to the north east.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: The one that leads to the aqueduct?! We'll have Fortis guards barging into the city if they catch wind...

steps.player: It sounds like you need help.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Cam Torum does not need help, much less that of any humans!

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Wake the off-duty guards and put them to work. I'll ensure they're paid handsomely.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I'm afraid we already have.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Argh! Get back to your post!

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Alright, fine! Human, you look like you've seen a fight or two. Deal with the escaped creature by the mountain outflow spring.

steps.player: Hang on, what's in it for me?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: What do you want?!

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Access to the city sounds nice.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Fine, get to it!

options.text: No.

steps.player: On secound thoughts, I don't like your attitude.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Then go away!

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: Have you killed that creature yet?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma-or-at.text: It's up by the mountain outflow spring, north east of here. Get to it before it makes its way to the aqueduct!

ruins-in-cam-torum-killing-the-sulphur-n.text: If the player is the primary person to kill the Nagua:

steps.player: I should head back to Attala and let her know that the aqueduct is secure.

ruins-in-cam-torum-killing-the-sulphur-n.text: If the player deals significant damage to the Nagua, which also receives damage from another player:

steps.player: Good work team! Let's let Attala know we all killed it, together!

ruins-in-cam-torum-killing-the-sulphur-n.text: If the player deals a small amount of damage to the Nagua, which is killed by another player:

steps.player: Technically I helped kill it... Without me, the others might have been overwhelmed... Yes... I should let Attala know the aqueduct is secure.

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.player: I've taken care of the... What was that thing anyway?

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: A spirit of sorts. Something far older than anything your people have bothered to remember. In any case, a deal is a deal. You may enter the city of Cam Torum.

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: Yes, and I'm not going anywhere!

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: Fine! If it'll make you stop pestering me, you can join...

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: [player name], he's your responsibility now. If either of you cause any trouble, you're both out!

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: Thank you, [player name]. I'm Zuma, by the way. I'll meet you inside.
The screen briefly fades to black, and Zuma disappears into the city.

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Builder 1
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: Thanks for that, mate. You should speak to Jess inside. She'll be in the north of the city. She could use a problem solver like yourself.

ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.speaker: Builder 2
ruins-in-cam-torum-returning-to-attala.text: She's the archaeologist in charge of the dig into these ruins they've found. Discovering the mysteries of the past and that.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: Thanks for that, mate. You should speak to Jess inside. She'll be in the north of the city. She could use a problem solver like yourself.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-the-builde.text: You should head inside, mate. Remember, Jess will be in the north of the city. She could use a problem solver like yourself.

ruins-in-cam-torum-walking-through-cam-t.player: I'm here to help, you know...

ruins-in-cam-torum-walking-through-cam-t.speaker: Citizen
ruins-in-cam-torum-walking-through-cam-t.text: Every day they let more of your kind in.

ruins-in-cam-torum-walking-through-cam-t.speaker: Citizen
ruins-in-cam-torum-walking-through-cam-t.text: Another human? Do what you need to and then be gone from here.

ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-enter-t.speaker: Jessamine
ruins-in-cam-torum-attempting-to-enter-t.text: Excuse me! I don't believe I've given you permission to enter the dig.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-attala.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-attala.text: Well with the suitation outside dealt with, I now need to keep an eye on this expedition. Any mistakes made in these ruins could bring the ground out from beneath our city!

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-attala.player: Is it really that dangerous in there?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-attala.speaker: Attala
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-attala.text: It might be if you don't know what you're dealing with. Your people often assume they do, which generally makes things worse.

options.text: The rest of your people don't seem very happy I'm here.

steps.player: The rest of your people don't seem very happy I'm here.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: The rest?! I'm not happy you're here either.

steps.player: I helped you with the aqueduct. You could afford to show a little bit of gratitude.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: You'll have my gratitude when you finish you business in Cam Torum and leave.

options.text: Will the city's defense be okay without you?

steps.player: Will the city's defense be okay without you?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: As I say, the situation has been dealt with for now. Besides, the only reason that situation existed in the first place is because of these ruins.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: At this point a smart person would call off this dig entirely, but as that doesn't seem set to happen, I'd say it's in our best interests we keep an eye on things.

options.text: I take it you don't get on well with the humans?

steps.player: I take it you don't get on well with the humans?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: It's not exactly that. You have your virtues, but you have short sight and even shorter memories, which can be very dangerous.

steps.player: Why not share what you know with us then?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: I suspect some of your people wouldn't be too pleased if we did. The truth isn't something that everyone desires.

steps.player: Well I'm always open to a bit of truth myself.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmph! I doubt that.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.text: Thank you for your help back there, [player name]. Dwarves can be very stubborn.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.text: It is not stubbornness on my part. It is duty that drives me.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-zuma.text: I am a nelta of Ranul and I am bound by his tenets. One of them is to ensure that knowledge is protected and respected. These ruins they've found could contain all manner of things! I must find out!

options.text: How did you hear about the ruins?

steps.player: How did you hear about these ruins?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: The cave-in that revealed them shook the foundations of the Teomat!

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: The dwarves tried to hide them from us, but we eventually found out.

options.text: What are you expecting to find down there?

steps.player: What are you expecting to find down there?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: I don't know exactly yet, but knowledge of some kind! Maybe even some undiscovered history regarding Ralos and Ranul!

options.text: I take it you don't get on well with the dwarves?

steps.player: I take it you don't get on well with the dwarves?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: They are arrogant! They think they know it all, and worst of all, they are non-believers!

steps.player: Technically I'm a non-believer.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: But that is because you are ignorant of the truth, not because you outright reject it. Would you like me to tell you of the ways of Ranul?

steps.player: Maybe some other time.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Timoiva.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.text: Nilsal! The name's Jessamine, though most people call me Jess. You must be [player name]. I hear you sorted out the situation holding back the arrivial of our supplies. Thanks for that.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.player: Don't mention it. So you're here for these ruins beneath the city?

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.text: Yes, a cave-in revealed them! I'm here to lead the dig and see what we can discover.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.player: There seems to be a lot of ancient ruins popping up lately.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine.text: Gielinor has been around for a long time. We're really only just starting to scratch its surface!

options.text: Can I be of any help with the dig?

steps.player: Can I be of any help with the dig?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Well it seems our expedition has already gained a couple of new recruits somehow, but what I really need is someone more proactive who can fend for themselves. You seem perfect for the job!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Meet me inside the ruins. We need help setting up some base camps for further exploration.

options.text: How come the dwarves let you in?

steps.player: How come the dwarves let you in?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: I work at the museum in Fortis. The dwarves have a begrudging alliance with the capital, and so they begrudgingly let me in.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: They demanded agreement to some absurdly expensive export deals in exchange, and even exclusive rights to some imports from the mainland.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: It took weeks of negotiation, and they still don't seem entirely satisfied.

steps.player: I take it you don't get on too well?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: No. It's a shame. They would be a great source of historical knowledge, if they were just more willing to share it.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: See you later.

ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine-.speaker: Jessamine
ruins-in-cam-torum-talking-to-jessamine-.text: Nilsal! When you're ready, meet me inside the ruins. We need help setting up some base camps for further exploration.

options.text: How come the dwarves let you in?
Goodbye.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-attempting-to-e.player: I should probably speak to the others before I go exploring.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.player: I'm surprised to see you both in such high spirits after walking past all those jeering dwarves.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 2
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: Ah, well it's unfortunate, but no reason to be sad. It's them that ought to be sad.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 1
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: Aye, mate. Livin' a life unable to connect with others because they look different must be miserable.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 2
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: We wish 'em the best. Hopefully their paths to personal growth are near and smooth.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Xali.... Ates... Hmm, no, not quite right...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: The moon blotting out the sun, could this be...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.text: This is an old place, [player name]. Older even than much of what we dwarves remember.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.text: No, it's dangerous is what it is.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.text: Now where is that fool priest?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: This is sacred ground. This is most obviously a shrine built by emissaries of Ranul.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: You see a picture of a creature eating the sun and instead of a warning, you see evidence of your god? You really are beyond saving.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: Enough! This mural may depict a scene straight from our holy scriptures! Show some respect!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.player: Alright, calm down, both of you. Let's go see what the actual archaeologist has to say.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: Attala and Zuma walk over to Jessamine

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Strange...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: This mural has an inscription beneath it, written in the language of the Old Ones. I think I'm getting there, but I'm going to need more time to decipher it.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: We don't need to be deciphering inscriptions to know that we shouldn't be here. I mean look at that... whatever that floating thing is. This place is dangerous!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: All the more reason to find out more about it then.
If the player has not completed The Garden of Death:

steps.player: Do you need me to do anything in the meantime?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: If the player has completed The Garden of Death:

steps.player: Could I help with the translations? I actually have a bit of experience with this language.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: That's very kind of you to offer, but if it's okay with you, I actually have a different task I could use your help with.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: The surrounding caverns are quite large. If you could take some building supplies and set up some camps in each of them, it would make further exploration a lot easier.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Have you finished setting up the camps?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Let me know when you have. In the meantime, I've got to keep working on this inscription, whilst also making sure these two don't kill each other...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: Speaking of which, what about you? Why a life of archaeology?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: I've always loved it. When I was a child, I had a friend in Fortis who I'd collect old trinkets with.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: It's right here! It clearly says...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: I see. I guess it was a natural next step then?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: I don't care what your book says! Your book won't keep us safe from...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Indeed. The employees at the museum already knew me well by the time I applied. I've spent a lot of my life browsing it.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: The last time you humans did something like this...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: You should visit the museum in Varrock some time. There's a lot to see!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Always 'you humans'. You do realise I am not my great-grandfather...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: I've been meaning to! Thing is, I couldn't turn down this opportunity when it came up.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Keep this up and I'll have you kicked out of the...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: Understandable. Right, I should get back to those camps.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: The secrets of this dungeon belong to the Varlamorian people! You can't...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: How can you make those claims so confidently?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: It's in the holy scriptures! As I was saying...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Can't get a word in edgeways with these two.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-attempting-to-e.player: I should grab the camp building supplies before I do any more exploration.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-taking-building.text: The following assumes that the player has not yet built any campsites. The player can only take as many building supplies as there are campsites left to build; the dialogue and item receipt amounts adjust accordingly if the player has built some but not all campsites.
If the player does not have sufficient inventory space:

steps.text: You don't have enough room to take everything you need from the crates. You need [one/two/three/four/five] free space[s].

remnants-of-the-old-ones-taking-building.text: If the player already has some building supplies:

steps.text: If the player has exactly one building supplies:
You take some supplies from the crates.

a hammer and/or spade if they do not have one in inventory
If the player has exactly two building supplies:
You take some supplies from the crates.
one Building supplies
a hammer and/or spade if they do not have one in inventory
If the player has three or more building supplies:
If the player does not have a hammer or a saw:
You take some supplies from the crates.
If the player has a hammer but not a saw:
You take some supplies from the crates.
You take some supplies from the crates.
You already have everything you need from these crates.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-taking-building.text: You take some supplies from the crates.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-attempting-to-e.player: This entrance looks dangerous. I probably shouldn't go in here without a good reason.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-trapping-rocks-.player: I probably shouldn't touch anything until the others have had a chance to look around.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 2
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: Thanks for taking care of those base camps, mate.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.player: No problem. I hope there's no hard feelings over Jessamine asking me to do a part of your jobs.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 1
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: That's no worries, mate, I've no issue admitting you're better cut out for building camps in dangerous dungeons than I am.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 2
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: We may not be mul'i-disciplined adventurers like you, but we don't need to be. The world needs more than just heroes, don't it?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 1
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: Aye, mate, I'm content and proud to just be a hard working, decent builder.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.speaker: Builder 2
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.text: Besides, without us, building supplies wouldn't be there in the first place. Life's all about working together.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-the-.player: Glad to hear it. Keep up the good work then!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: I've finished setting up the camps.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Thanks. I'm all done deciphering the inscription. Some of it has worn away, so we're missing bits, but between it, the murals and the big floating monolith, we've already found some pretty exciting stuff!

options.text: What does the inscription say?

steps.player: What does the inscription say?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: 'Here in Neypotzli, by ??? of earth and streams, have these emissaries of ??? been sealed, ??? ??? ???.'

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Emissaries of Ranul! We must work to free them at once.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: First they built the place, now they're sealed in it. These leaping assumptions are going to get us all killed!

steps.player: Well I've only ever had good experiences opening ancient vaults.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Attala is right to be cautious. These murals don't look all too friendly...

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: But these emissaries may have ancient knowledge lost to the ages! We must investigate further.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: These ruins are directly beneath the Teomat... I suppose it's possible there may be some links to Ralos and Ranul.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: I will not allow you to put Cam Torum in danger just because you're curious!

steps.player: I'm not sure if these disagreements are really getting us anywhere...

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: You make a good point.

options.text: What do we do now?

steps.player: What do we do now?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: I think it would be unwise to go and start freeing emissaries that we know nothing about.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Agreed!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: But we should still try and learn more about them. They may pose a risk to Cam Torum.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmph! Very well.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: We know they were sealed by the power of earth and streams. This magic presumably originates from somewhere within these ruins. I also wonder if these talismans I found might be connected...
Jessamine shows you an earth and a water talisman.

steps.player: Interesting...

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmm... Nahta will know what to do with these. [player name], take them to him in Cam Torum's magic shop. Tell him I sent you.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Come back to me when you have space and I'll give you the talismans.
Jessamine hands you the talismans.

options.text: What does the western mural depict?
What does the eastern mural depict?

Goodbye.
What does the western mural depict?

steps.player: What does the western mural depict?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: It's raining blood! It is clearly a depiction of death!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: It's not clear from the mural whether the creature depicted is calling the rain or lamenting its arrival.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: It's an emissary of the blood moon! A bringer of rain and bountiful harvests!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Blood moons don't usually bring good harvests, and I don't see any thriving crops depicted in the mural.

steps.player: So what do you make of it?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: You cannot deny us the Blood Moon's bounty!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: The blood moon is nothing more than a cosmic occurrence. We need more context to come to any conclusions.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Cam Torum has no interest in bathing in blood!

options.text: What does the eastern mural depict?

steps.player: What does the eastern mural depict?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: An emissary of the eclipsed moon! A herald of Ximoua!

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Ximoua? It is eating the sun, you fool! If it's a herald of anything, it's death!

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Given what is taught about Ximoua, that isn't too surprising.

options.text: What is Ximoua again?

steps.player: What is Ximoua again?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: An eclipse that marks the end of a cycle! The destruction of the world and its rebirth!

steps.player: Ah yes, I remember now. Very pleasant.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Indeed, it is an event we all look forward to. It is said that when it happens, Ralos and Ranul unite all life as one! Can you imagine such an honour?

options.text: Maybe we should focus on something else.

steps.player: Maybe we should focus on something else.

options.text: What does the northern mural depict?

steps.player: What does the northern mural depict?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: A creature snapping a mountain in half. Care to explain this one, Zuma?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: It's an emissary of the blue moon! Clearly... er... bringing an end to the winter?

steps.player: Any thoughts on this one, Jess?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Blue moons are exceedinly rare... They're only seen occasionally during volcanic eruptions. It's possible that this cracking mountain signals the appearance of a volcano.

options.text: Goodbye.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: You'll need to make some space for those two talismans [player name].

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Do you have the enchanted talismans yet?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Let Attala know if you need any help.

options.text: Good job mediating those two.

steps.player: Good job mediating those two.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Thanks. It does feel a bit like I'm walking a tightrope over a scorpion nest at times.

steps.player: Attala might be worse than a pit of scorpions!

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Did I hear my name?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Yes! We were just saying how helpful you've been!

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: Quite!

options.text: So how did you end up getting assigned to these ruins?

steps.player: So how did you end up getting assigned to these ruins?

steps.speaker: Jessamine
steps.text: The museum suspected there might be an Old One connection. It's one of my specialties, so exploring these kinds of places is what I do.

options.text: Goodbye.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-atta.text: Take the talismans to Nahta in Cam Torum's magic shop. Tell him I sent you.

steps.player: What if I lost them?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Then you'll need to find some more yourself, and take better care with them once you have!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: Any word on the enchanted talismans?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-zuma.text: I'm afraid you'll need to talk to Attala if you need any help.

options.text: What lead you to be such a devout follower of Ranul?

steps.player: What lead you to be such a devout follower of Ranul?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Ralos appeals to many who wish to live fast-paced lives.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: I do see that appeal, but there is a calmness and peace in Ranul that calls to me.

steps.player: Doesn't Ranul govern over death? That doesn't put you off?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Making peace with death is one of the things that attracted me to Ranul's teachings.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: That, and all the time I get to spend in nice and quiet libraries.

options.text: So is this place what you were expecting?

steps.player: So is this place what you were expecting?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Far more so! As much as Attala refuses to believe it, I think these ruins are connected to Ranul.

steps.player: Is it because of all the moon symbology?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: That's part of it, but there's also that thing at the centre of this room. Some of the markings remind me of something I once read about.

steps.player: Interesting, if a bit vague. Care to elaborate on what it is you read about?

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: I can't really. I'm still not done putting my theory together.

steps.player: Well I look forward to hearing more once you've done so.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Zuma
steps.text: Timoiva.

options.text: Yes please.
Where do you get your runes from?
Actually, I've been sent by Attala.

steps.player: Actually, I've been sent by Attala.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: Attala? Why's that?

steps.player: We're trying to find out more about a source of magic in the ruins beneath the city. She asked me to bring some talismans to you.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: If she needs me to get involved, then no doubt this is something well beyond your people and probably highly dangerous.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: But I suppose if she's okay with that... Go on then, let's have a look.

steps.player: Er... I seem to have misplaced them.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: Then you'd better go and find them.
You show the talismans to Nahta.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: How in the... Where did you get these?

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: Actually, on second thoughts, I'm not sure I want to know.
Nahta casts a spell on the talismans.

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: There. Now take them to the blacksmith. Tell him they've been enchanted to react to naguanil magic and they need some finishing touches.

options.text: Naguanil? What's that?

steps.player: Naguanil? What's that?

steps.speaker: Nahta
steps.text: A type of magic your people have forgotten, alongside many other things. I don't have time to catch you up on the history of the word though, so you'll need to learn more somewhere else.

options.text: Okay, thanks for the help.

steps.player: Okay, thanks for the help.

options.text: No thanks.

steps.player: The owner of the magic shop said something about these talismans detecting... aguatil?

steps.text: Naguanil. Hmm...

options.text: Can you help?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.text: I am Eyatlalli, a nagua of earth and streams.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.player: Right... And what is this place?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.text: For the Moons of Peril, and their long dead summoner.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.text: Yes. Powerful and terrible nagua summoned to wreak havoc.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.player: Why would anyone want to do that?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.text: In the face of inevitable death, a powerful shaman decided to lash out and inflict death on others.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-locating-the-ta.text: Her fellows disagreed with her actions. They created this prison, and they summoned me to watch over it.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: I am Eyatlalli, a nagua of-

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: The icosahedron has been disturbed.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Icosahedron. An object of twenty facets, floating at the centre of this room.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: Did anybody touch that thing whilst I was gone?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Zuma did something. We were discussing the murals and when we turned around, he was gone!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Attala
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: I knew I shouldn't have let that fool priest in!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: It is key to the magics that keep the Moons of Peril contained. It reshapes and reweaves the magical seals as the Moons attempt to break them.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.player: Isn't it a good thing it moved then?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: For it to have moved means that the seals must have needed reshaping. That has not happened for decades.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Zuma must have done something!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: For centuries, the magic used to seal the Moons has been woven into Neypotzli and the creatures that inhabit it.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Naguanil is the magic of nature. A ritual involving the living parts of this place could re-infuse the icosahedron.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Living parts? As in the animals?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: Yes. Bring me scales of a bream, the tail of a moss lizard and paste made of moonlight grubs. I will begin preparing the rest of the ritual.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Jessamine
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: [player name], what's going on?!

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-jess.text: The Moons of Peril rage against their bindings. Holding them back is exhausting. Please bring me the bream scales, moss lizard tail and moonlight grub paste from elsewhere in Neypotzli.

options.text: Where can I find bream?

steps.player: Where can I find bream?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: They can be fished in the north east section of Neypotzli.

options.text: Where can I find moss lizards?

steps.player: Where can I find moss lizards?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: They can be caught in the north west section of Neypotzli. They'll likely be hiding in the bushes.

options.text: Where can I find moonlight grubs?

steps.player: Where can I find moonlight grubs?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: They can be picked off of the saplings growing all around the north of Neypotzli.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Place the scales in the shape of the sun at high noon.
You place the scales in the shape of the sun.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Place the lizard tail beneath it as the earth.
You place the lizard tail beneath the sun.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Now carve the earth in two with the paste, as the stream carves the earth.
You pull the tail apart and draw a line through it with the paste.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: The ritual is in motion, but the wound to the seal will not close with the Moons still raging against it. I must ask you for one more small favour.
If the player has completed One Small Favour:

steps.player: Please, no...

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: The Moons cannot be killed, but they can be distracted whilst I repair the seal. Enter their chambers here in Neypotzli and engage them in combat.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.player: Aren't these things like unstoppable forces of nature or something? Am I going to be alright in there?

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Ordinarily, no. Their mere presence is enough to bring most creatures to an early death. However, you have my help.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Whilst you fight them, look for my glyphs. They will protect and guide you. If the Moons become too enraged, I will transport you out of their chambers.

options.text: Could you remind me what your glyphs look like?

steps.player: Could you remind me what your glyphs look like?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Here. This is what to look for.
Eyatlalli creates a glyph on the floor where the player is standing

options.text: What should I expect from the Blood Moon?

steps.player: What should I expect from the Blood Moon?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: When it starts to rain blood, look to your feet. When the jaguars are summoned, prepare to leap back.

options.text: What should I expect from the Blue Moon?

steps.player: What should I expect from the Blue Moon?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Be prepared to fight without your weapon. Ensure the room's braziers remain lit, for the cold will restore the Moon's strength.

options.text: What should I expect from the Eclipse Moon?

steps.player: What should I expect from the Eclipse Moon?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Ensure it doesn't catch you with your back turned. Make sure to take cover when it fires its searing hot rays.

options.text: Anything else I should know?

steps.player: Anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Any time the Moons of Peril inflict pain, they can heal themselves, freeze your joints, or blind your eyes. A defensive approach should be used against them.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: If the player lost the lizard tail:

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: The Moons of Peril rage against their bindings. Holding them back is exhausting. Please bring me the moss lizard tail and moonlight grub paste from elsewhere in Neypotzli

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Place the lizard tail beneath it as the earth.
If the player lost the grub paste:

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: The Moons of Peril rage against their bindings. Holding them back is exhausting. Please bring me the moonlight grub paste from elsewhere in Neypotzli.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: Now carve the earth in two with the paste, as the stream carves the earth.

remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.speaker: Eyatlalli
remnants-of-the-old-ones-talking-to-eyat.text: The ritual is in motion, but the wound to the seal will not close with the Moons still raging against it. I must ask you for one more small favour.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-jessamine.text: It is, although I'd be lying if I didn't admit that it is also fascinating.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-jessamine.text: Naguanil magic, ancient spirits of nature... This is the discovery of the century!

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-jessamine.player: Let's make sure that Cam Torum is safe before we start celebrating.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-attala.speaker: Attala
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-attala.text: After berating you about keeping an eye on the priest, I failed to do the same myself. I was caught up in the mystery.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-attala.speaker: Attala
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-attala.text: Perhaps there's a little human in me after all!

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-attala.player: It's okay, we'll figure this out.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.player: You seem remarkably calm considering everything that's going on.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 2
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.text: Life's unpredictable, mate. No sense stressin' over what's out of your control.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.text: It's not like we're not aware of the danger we're in, but worryin' about it ain't productive.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.player: Shouldn't you be getting out of here if you feel like you're in danger?

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 2
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.text: We may not be in total control of our surroundings, but we can still impact them positively through our actions. Like bein' here to support you.

the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.speaker: Builder 1
the-moons-of-peril-talking-to-the-builde.text: Even if that's just emotionally. We believe in you, mate.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blue-mo.text: Eyatlalli's voice echoes through the surrounding earth.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blue-mo.speaker: Eyatlalli
the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blue-mo.text: Thank you, iknil. The Blue Moon of Peril is sufficiently distracted. You should now proceed on to the next one.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blood-m.text: Eyatlalli's voice echoes through the surrounding earth.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blood-m.speaker: Eyatlalli
the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-blood-m.text: Thank you, iknil. The Blood Moon of Peril is sufficiently distracted. You should now proceed on to the next one.

the-moons-of-peril-encountering-the-ecli.text: A cutscene begins. Zuma is seen approaching the Eclipse Moon.

the-moons-of-peril-encountering-the-ecli.speaker: Zuma
the-moons-of-peril-encountering-the-ecli.text: I can't believe it... An emissary of my god, standing before me...
The Eclipse Moon attacks Zuma, nearly killing him.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-eclipse.text: Eyatlalli's voice echoes through the surrounding earth.

the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-eclipse.speaker: Eyatlalli
the-moons-of-peril-defeating-the-eclipse.text: Thank you, iknil. Eclipse Moon of Peril is sufficiently distracted. You should now proceed on to the next one.

the-moons-of-peril-attempting-to-enter-t.player: I've done everything I need to here. I should check in with Eyatlalli.

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.speaker: Builder 1
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.text: You meant well. You thought you were helpin'. Can't fault you for that part, mate.

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.speaker: Builder 2
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.text: You made a mistake. Coulda been any of us. Just gotta make sure we learn from our mistakes is all.

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.speaker: Builder 1
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.text: And if yer genuinely sorry, best you can do is work to be better, not mope around. So keep your chin up, mate!

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.speaker: Zuma
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.text: I saw sun and moon runes on that thing. Recalled something from Ranul's teachings, a rite he once performed...

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.speaker: Zuma
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.text: I tried to emulate it, and it worked. I thought I had freed his emissaries. But they weren't that at all...

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-or-the-buil.player: Interesting. Maybe there was some sort of connection between Ranul and this place after all.

finishing-up-talking-to-jessamine-after-.speaker: Jessamine
finishing-up-talking-to-jessamine-after-.text: Good work, [player name]. We made many significant discoveries today, even if it was a bit precarious.

finishing-up-talking-to-jessamine-after-.speaker: Jessamine
finishing-up-talking-to-jessamine-after-.text: I'll be sticking around here for some time I reckon. There's still so much to discover in this place. See you around.

finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.speaker: Attala
finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.text: The nagua seems to have relaxed. I assume you were successful?

finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.speaker: Attala
finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.text: You have my gratitude, [player name]. You have helped to ensure Cam Torum's safety. You will always be welcome back.

finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.player: Something tells me the rest of your people won't be too happy about that.

finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.speaker: Attala
finishing-up-talking-to-attala-after-def.text: Well it's not their choice, so they'll just have to suck it up. Who knows, maybe given long enough, you might start to grow on them!

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-again.speaker: Zuma
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-again.text: I suppose I should think about heading back to the Teomat. I might not mention everything that happened down here to the others...

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-again.speaker: Zuma
finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-again.text: I suppose I still have plenty to share. Maybe I'll write a book about it!

finishing-up-talking-to-zuma-again.player: I'm sure it will be a great one. Until next time, Zuma.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-builders-aga.speaker: Builder 1
finishing-up-talking-to-the-builders-aga.text: Well, all's well that ends well.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-builders-aga.speaker: Builder 2
finishing-up-talking-to-the-builders-aga.text: We never had any doubts! Always knew you'd get it sorted, mate.

finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.speaker: Eyatlalli
finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.text: You have done well. The seal is repaired, but the Moons have seen a glimpse of freedom. Even now they rage against their bindings. It is... taxing.

finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.speaker: Eyatlalli
finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.text: You could. Distracting them again will afford me some rest. In return, I am willing to repay you with trinkets from ancient times.

finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.speaker: Eyatlalli
finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.text: Very well. Come and claim your rewards from the chamber to the south east. Should you aid in containing them again, you can return there to receive more rewards.

finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.speaker: Eyatlalli
finishing-up-talking-to-eyatlalli-after-.text: For now though, thank you for your help, iknil.

options.text: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.player: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: No.

steps.player: Care to explain further?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Does the stream tire of eroding the earth? Does the earth tire of forming the mountain?

steps.player: Not that I can tell.

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: I have more in common with them than I do with most of your kind, iknil. Think of me as you do them.

options.text: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.player: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: It is a prison. Everything around us serves that purpose.

steps.player: Even the plants and the streams?

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: I am a nagua of earth and stream. Being close to both empowers me to do my task.

steps.speaker: Eyatlalli
steps.text: Just as being far from moonlight weakens the Moons of Peril.

options.text: Goodbye.

steps.player: Goodbye.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.speaker: Builder 1
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.text: Good to see you again, mate.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.player: Good to see you both as well. How's things?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.speaker: Builder 2
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.text: Never better, mate. Never better. This here ruin was the find of the century!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.speaker: Builder 1
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-build.text: All credit to Jess, o'course, but we're glad to be doing our bit!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.text: Nilsal, [player name]. How are things going?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.player: Pretty good, thanks. How about you? Made any more discoveries down here?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.speaker: Jessamine
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.text: More than you can count! I've found so much new information on the Old Ones and naguanil. The museum are hoping to include it all in some new exhibits soon!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-jessamine.player: Sounds awesome! I'll be sure to keep an eye out for them. On that note, I'll let you get back to it.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-attalla.speaker: Attala
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-attalla.text: Hello there, [player name]. What can I do for you?

options.text: How are things?

steps.player: How are things?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Now that the situation in the ruins is under control, things are nice and quiet, which is just what we need. That whole business down there got a lot of dwarves riled up.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Naturally, most blame you humans.

steps.player: Of course. Have you tried explaining to them that we actually helped?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Ha! Good one. You think I'm going to make a laughing stock of myself by daring to claim a human did something positive? Keep dreaming!

options.text: So how long has Cam Torum been around?

steps.player: So how long has Cam Torum been around?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: What am I, a historian?

steps.player: No, but you're the only dwarf here that might be willing to share that sort of information with me.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmph. Very well. The Varlamorians won't mention this, but we were the first to settle here. Our ancestors saw the writing on the wall when Xeric came to power in Kourend. They chose not to stick around.

steps.player: Must have been a big thing for them, leaving their home.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Doubtful. My people are all too familiar with that sort of thing. The Lovakengj dwarves have mostly forgotten their history, but we Dwarves of Cam Torum remember it all too well.

steps.player: Remember what?

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Before Lovakengj, there was Imcandoria. Our ancestors there were forced to abandon their home, just as we were forced to leave Kourend.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: If you humans had had your way, we might have had to abandon Cam Torum by now as well.

steps.player: You don't know that.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: But I do know that. As I said, we remember our history, and we know that those who don't are doomed to repeat it.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: The Varlamorians nearly destroyed themselves in their War of Betrayal, but it was not them who were betrayed, it was us.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: I was a young dwarf when their war risked destroying our home. I saw the results of their pride. Meanwhile, they've all but forgotten it.

steps.player: Sorry. I didn't mean to dig up old wounds.

steps.speaker: Attala
steps.text: Hmph. It's fine. Your intentions are good, [player name], which is more than can be said for most of your kind. Who knows, maybe one or two dwarves here might even grow to tolerate you.

options.text: I'd better get going.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.text: A lot less stressful up here. I think I might leave the adventuring to people like you from now on.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.text: Still, at least it gave me a lot to talk about. Those Moons of Peril are concerning, but exciting! I just wish we knew more about their potential links to Ranul.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.player: So you still think there is a link?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.text: Oh yes. It may not have been the one I originally thought, but there must be something! They're called Moons after all!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.text: The all-powerful Ranul wouldn't have just let some random creatures take on a name like that!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.speaker: Zuma
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-zuma.text: Indeed. And on that note, I have some research to do! Until next time.

KSopRL.speaker: Blacksmith
KSopRL.text: Make some room if you want my help!

nnXC7t.speaker: Eyatlalli
nnXC7t.text: Thank you, iknil. The Moons are sufficiently distracted. You should now return to me.
